children: LIC’s complaint alleges misrepresentation and diversion of funds invested in five NCDs issued by Reliance Capital between 2012 and 2018

Reliance Group chairman Anil Ambani has denied any wrongdoing after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a case against Reliance Capital (RCAP) over an alleged Rs 2,684.57-crore fraud involving investments made by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The FIR names RCAP, its former chairman, former group managing director Satish Seth, unidentified public servants and others.

The FIR was registered on the basis of a written complaint received from LIC, according to an official statement. The case relates to investments made by the insurer in RCAP and allegations including cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal misconduct, diversion or misappropriation of funds and falsification of accounts.

A spokesperson for Ambani said the FIR pertains to Reliance Capital and noted that Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director and Chairman of the company’s board from 2005 until November 2021. At that time, the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an Administrator.

Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law, the spokesperson added. The CBI’s case, meanwhile, concerns the allegations made in LIC’s complaint against RCAP, Ambani, Seth, unidentified public servants and others.

According to the CBI, LIC has alleged that it subscribed to five non-convertible debentures issued by RCAP between 12 April 2012, and 9 March 2018. The investments aggregated to Rs 3,900 crore and were made for general corporate purposes, funding requirements and refinancing of existing debt.

The CBI said LIC has alleged that the accused persons entered into a criminal conspiracy and committed offences including cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal misconduct, diversion or misappropriation of funds and falsification of accounts. These allegations form part of the complaint on which the FIR was registered.

LIC has alleged that the accused persons dishonestly induced it to invest in RCAP through misrepresentation and thereafter fraudulently diverted the funds. According to the CBI, the insurer has alleged that these actions resulted in a wrongful loss to LIC.

The CBI said LIC has alleged that the acts caused a wrongful loss of Rs 2,684.57 crore to the insurer. The complaint also alleges a corresponding wrongful gain to the accused persons and other beneficiaries, according to the agency.

The CBI has taken up an investigation to identify the role of all those involved, including public servants and private individuals. The agency will also examine the alleged criminal conspiracy and trace the end-use or diversion of the invested funds.

The investigation covers the funds invested by LIC through the five NCDs issued by RCAP. The CBI said it would examine the allegations made in the complaint and trace the end-use or possible diversion of those investments.

The case remains under investigation, with the CBI examining the role of the individuals and entities named in the FIR. The agency’s probe will also cover the alleged criminal conspiracy and the movement of the funds invested by LIC.

The CBI said it had earlier registered eight FIRs against Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Capital Limited, Reliance Home Finance Limited, Reliance Commercial Finance Limited and Reliance Telecom Limited. The cases were based on complaints received from various public-sector banks, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and LIC.

The agency said it has so far filed six charge sheets and arrested seven accused persons in these cases. The CBI added that the cases remain under investigation and are being monitored by the Supreme Court.
